name: scale_field
title: Scale-space field on the momentum cohort
not_a_phase: BRIEF.md: 'This is not a phase prompt and does not want to become one.' The method has ~one free parameter, so there is nothing to pre-register. Correctness is enforced by research/scale_field/test_scale_field.py, which is the specification. What is kept from the standard: numbered decisions append-only, the evidence standard, the frozen cohort with its hash asserted, segment stratification, D4, 'the artifact wins'. The moment anything here touches forward returns, the full standard applies again.

cohort.rule: FROZEN. Phase 10 manifest, reused, never redrawn or extended. Hash asserted on every run.
cohort.hard_stop_on_mismatch: reconciliation stop -- the only escalation this brief carries beyond the Allan gate

read_path.rule: ZERO passes over filtered_trades / filtered_quotes. Every tick read is a targeted per-event parquet read, reusing research/phase_10/common.py:read_event_trades unchanged.
read_path.tie_order: sequence_number, ascending; never inverts under the sip sort

analysis_clock.decision: D3 -- extended-day analysis clock, America/New_York, DST-aware
analysis_clock.timezone_rule: segment assignment computed in America/New_York from the pinned XNYS calendar, never by casting the UTC sip_timestamp to a date
analysis_clock.segment_partition_rule: premarket [04:00, rth_open) | rth [rth_open, rth_close) | post [rth_close, post_end). The three tile the extended session exactly and are disjoint; the adapter test asserts it.

segments_not_poolable.rule: premarket and rth are reported separately, never pooled.
segments_not_poolable.evidence: v3 measured 0.903 decades of separation between premarket and regular hours (failure row 5).
segments_not_poolable.note: Two distinct segment notions are in play and are never conflated: the EVENT-level detection segment (det_segment_poll1, where the D7 anchor fell) stratifies events; the PRINT-level segment slices one event's tape by wall clock. The adapter exposes the second; the manifest carries the first.

d4.rule: Tick-derived only. No spine numeric column on any computation path.

reconciliation.rule: allan_factor() must reproduce v3's committed curve rung for rung. HARD STOP on divergence -- any divergence means the point-process handling differs from v3's and everything after it is uninterpretable.
reconciliation.window_origin: the D3 extended session [04:00 ET, post_end); windows tile the full in-window session so empty stretches are real zeros
reconciliation.tolerance_note: Exact float reproduction is the bar, not an approximate one -- both paths run the same arithmetic on the same integers. The tolerance exists only to absorb float association order.
reconciliation.v3_knees_role: WITHDRAWN AS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, 2026-08-28, by Cooper at the step-4 read. The brief made v3's knees a prediction the continuous field had to change character near. Cooper tested both candidate summary statistics against known injected truth and neither recovers a timescale at the scales this cohort lives at: pooled amplitude vs scale does not select scale at all (pins to the finest grid point for every tau over a 25x span); the local ridge tracks then degrades (recovered/injected 1.55, 0.99, 0.59, 0.18 for tau = 2, 8, 32, 128 s); the Allan knee has no stable conversion (tau-to-knee 8, 12.8, 5.1 over the same span). So a knee disagreement is two uncalibrated statistics being compared, not a finding. The knees remain recorded as v3's committed measurement. What the brief should have asked for is a recovery test against known truth -- Cooper's step 3, not started.
reconciliation.what_the_gate_actually_tested: The bit-exact Allan reproduction stands and was a good gate -- on the POINT-PROCESS PLUMBING, which is what it tests. That is unaffected by the withdrawal above.

scale_axis.rule: The scale axis is a continuum; these arrays are quadrature for plotting, not a kernel grid in the method.
scale_axis.hard_floor_note: 2^-20 s = 0.954 us, ~12x the 80.5 ns median timestamp resolution (49 ns min). Below it you are measuring quantization.

fine.coverage: +/- 15 s around the D7 detection anchor, read with +/- 15 min of context
fine.why_not_session_wide: > 110 s/event, impractical. The fragmentation scale lives at the fine end and does not need session-wide coverage; the coarse end is cheap and does.
fine.window_deviation_from_brief: THE BRIEF SAYS +/- 15 MIN; THIS RUNS +/- 15 s OF CHARTED WINDOW INSIDE A +/- 15 MIN READ. Recorded, not silently taken. A heatmap column cannot be narrower than its kernel or the panel draws sub-pixel structure as noise. Over 1,800 s a ~1,400-column chart gives 1.3 s per column, against a smallest kernel of 15.6 ms -- so the bottom six octaves of the fine band alias, and the first render duly showed a picket fence. The honest window for a band reaching 15.6 ms is W x 15.6 ms ~ 22 s. At +/- 15 s with 1,500 grid points the spacing is 20 ms, which resolves the floor, and the top scale (1 s) still spans 30 kernel widths. The +/- 15 min of tape is still READ, so the estimator has full context either side and the edge mask never bites inside the charted window. Compute cost is unchanged -- it is set by the pyramid's bin count over the read window, not by the grid -- so the brief's 7 s/event budget still holds.

scale_axis.coarse_cap_rule: session_span / 8. STATED, not silently applied: at s = 4096 s a regular-hours session (~23,400 s) holds ~2 independent windows, which is where v3's headline A = 1,245 sits. The 2048 s ceiling is below the cap for the extended session (57,600/8 = 7,200 s) and below it for RTH alone (23,400/8 = 2,925 s).

field.neff_rule: field() returns NaN under n_eff >= 8 and MUST NEVER be given a fallback. Same treatment as insufficient_context.
field.tie_variant: collapse_same_timestamp -- consecutive prints sharing a timestamp collapse to one arrival (reference variant, config/phase_10_v4.json)
field.t_grid_rule: Grid spacing must be <= the band's smallest scale, or the field is sampled below its own resolution and every chart of it aliases. coarse: 57,600 s / 900 = 64 s per column against a 1 s smallest scale -- the coarse heatmap is therefore ALSO under-sampled at its fine end and is read as a coarse-scale picture only. fine: 30 s / 1,500 = 20 ms against 15.6 ms.

poisson_null.status: UNIT-TEST FIXTURE ONLY. Never a threshold on this data.
poisson_null.why: The constant is exact for a Poisson process and this tape is nowhere near Poisson: Phase 10 v3 measured the Allan factor at 5.99 at T = 15.6 ms rising monotonically to 1,245 at T = 4,096 s. A z-score against Poisson would be inflated by roughly sqrt(A(T)) -- about 2.4x at milliseconds and ~35x at the hour scale.
poisson_null.replacement: Rate-matched inhomogeneous Poisson realisations simulated from each event's own intensity estimate, with that event's duration and timestamp quantisation. Machinery already specified in prompts/phase_10b.md T3c (200 draws, 2.5/97.5 percentile band, reported as a family over the bandwidth rather than one band) and already implemented in research/phase_10b/pipeline.py. REUSE IT; DO NOT REBUILD IT.
poisson_null.gated_on: step 5 of the brief's order of work -- after Cooper reads the single-event chart.

charts.grammar: extends research/phase_10d_diag1/plot_boundary_through_time.py, recorded as reusable for exactly this, with the kernel-scale axis replacing the boundary track

order_of_work: 1. adapter.py, plus a test that loads one known event and asserts monotone, positive, in-session timestamps.
2. Allan reconciliation against v3. HARD STOP on divergence.
3. One event, both bands, both channels. Chart it and STOP.
5. Only then: matched-null thresholds, then the cohort.
forward_returns: NOT TOUCHED. The moment anything here touches forward returns, the full Agent_Prompt_Standard applies again, pre-registered, no exceptions.

resolution_floor.derived_not_adopted: This is the estimator's own effective sample size rearranged. It is not a literature-adopted cutoff and there is no parameter in it to argue about.

measured_2026_08_28.best_reachable_event: SOS_2021-02-17_34.12, 831,614 prints, at its best 5% of session

resolution_floor.status: DESCRIPTIVE. No gate is proposed and none is applied. Whether an applicability gate should exist is an open Cooper decision (10c open item 4, 10d s4).
resolution_floor.usable_range_rule: A window bounds the scale axis from ABOVE as well as from below: the estimator masks within edge_scales = 4 kernel widths of each end, so a window of length W admits only s < W/8. Usable range = log10(s_max / s_min). Measured 2026-08-28 at the median lambda: anchor+10s 0.67 decades (2.2 octaves), anchor+60s 1.21 (4.0), anchor+300s 1.71 (5.7), full session 2.59 (8.6).
resolution_floor.premise_challenge: OPEN, and it is a challenge to the premise this build started from. A continuous scale axis is bought for automatic scale SELECTION, which needs decades to select across. At 2-4 octaves inside the operational window there is very little to select over, and three or four fixed kernels with matched-null bands would carry almost the same information at a fraction of the machinery. What the field still earns: s_min(t) fell out of the construction and produced the cohort finding; localisation in time is unaffected by a short scale range; and the floor is time-varying, so a fixed-kernel scheme would need s_min(t) anyway. Step 3 must answer this, not assume it.

step_3_recovery_grid.status: PRE-REGISTERED, NOT STARTED -- AND NOW DECISIVE (D23). D22 declined it on the grounds that the onset test was negative and the fixed-kernel arm was the likely winner rather than a control. The onset test is no longer negative, so that reasoning lapses.
step_3_recovery_grid.supersedes: both earlier aims. 1-300 s was wrong at both ends: 300 s does not fit inside a tradeable window at this horizon class, and 1 s is below the floor for a large share of events at the shorter windows.
step_3_recovery_grid.lambda_why: the OBSERVED near-anchor regime (anchor+300s, +60s, +10s median lambda), not the session-mean one.

whether the continuum beats three fixed kernels in a one-decade band
step_3_recovery_grid.consequence_if_it_does_not: the deliverable is the resolution floor plus a small fixed-kernel rate statistic -- cheaper and more defensible than a scale-space field.

task_1_lead_time.status: DONE 2026-08-28. Negative on the operational claim.
task_1_lead_time.question: does the parameter-free field boolean LEAD a level detector, or restate it?
task_1_lead_time.field: sign of dL/dln s at the smallest ladder scale clearing 2*s_min(t)
task_1_lead_time.level: lambda_hat(t,s*) above its own trailing q90 over a causal 300 s lookback
task_1_lead_time.sign_correction: the work order specifies dL/dln s > 0, which on this estimator selects VOIDS (dL/dln s = E_w[z^2]-1 -> -1 inside a cluster). Measured: negative at 14/14 scales inside a synthetic burst. Both orientations reported; < 0 is primary because LEVEL is a high-activity detector.
controls_added: debounce at one kernel width, applied to BOTH booleans
match tolerance tied to FIELD's own onset spacing, not to s
circular-shift null, 200 draws/event, count and spacing preserved
task_1_lead_time.reading: NOT a restatement (Jaccard 0.26 vs a 0.9 bar; R^2 0.18) and NOT a lead -- it LAGS. Field fires first on 29.7% of matched onsets against a 50% chance baseline. Cooper's pre-fixed read was that firing at the same instants means the construction adds nothing operationally; the measured answer is worse than that.
task_1_lead_time.what_survives: the parameter-free construction is still a real structural gain -- zero is not a tunable and 2.26 is not a cutoff -- and the field is still distinct from a rate detector. Distinct and earlier are different properties and only the second was tradeable.
task_1_lead_time.consequence: Tasks 2-5 NOT STARTED. Task 1 was specified as deciding the rest. Task 3's fixed-kernel control arm is now MORE important, not less.

divergence_test.sign_form: DEGENERATE on real tape: median D at s* is -1.29 decades below the Poisson identity, so D<0 is ON ~100% and emits 4 onsets over 75 events.
divergence_test.relative_form: D below its own trailing q10. Lead +0.229 s-units but binomial p=0.349 on n=41 from 20/75 events -- not distinguishable from chance -- and not parameter-free.
divergence_test.kill_condition: MET. The construction closes as a detector; only s_min survives.

status: REOPENED IN PART 2026-08-30 -- D23. D22's structural fact 2 does not survive the causal re-derivation; fact 1 (saturation) and the s_min deliverable do.
closing_decision: D22 (2026-08-28), amended by D23 (2026-08-30). Next free number D24.
one_sided_kernel_precondition: STANDING, UNDISCHARGED. Both booleans use a CENTRED kernel and read forward by ~s. Relative ordering survives; NO ABSOLUTE TIMING CLAIM DOES. Nothing in this line is tradeable until the construction is re-derived on a one-sided kernel and the comparison re-run. Recorded in D22.

one_sided_kernel.supersedes_field: one_sided_kernel_precondition, which stated it as UNDISCHARGED.
one_sided_kernel.kernel: half-Gaussian w(u) = exp(-u^2/2s^2) * 1[u >= 0], u = t - t_i
one_sided_kernel.nothing_to_pre_register: The causal variant introduces NO new tunable. It is a support restriction; every constant that changes is derived from it, not chosen: Z(s) = s*sqrt(pi/2), n_eff = sqrt(pi)*s*lambda, s_min = 4.5135/lambda. The brief's 'there is nothing to pre-register' therefore still holds, and this block is a RECORD of what ran, written after the run, not a parameter committed before it.

derived_constants.relation: one-sided n_eff is EXACTLY half, so s_min is EXACTLY double

one_sided_kernel.unchanged_by_the_swap: dw/dln s = w*z^2 (the indicator does not depend on s), so dL/dln s = E_w[z^2] - 1 and the -1 BOUND SURVIVES. D22 structural fact 1 is NOT repaired by going causal -- only fact 2, the centring, is addressed. The Poisson cross-channel identity also survives.
one_sided_kernel.implementation: scale_field.field_onesided -- explicit FFT convolution, NO pyramid. Half-Gaussians do not compose in quadrature, and the pyramid's symmetric pre-decimation low-pass would leak future into past by ~1 bin. The causal path therefore carries STRICTLY FEWER approximations than the centred path it is compared against.
one_sided_kernel.causality_convention: field evaluated at bin RIGHT edges, so a print in bin b' reaches output bin b only when b' <= b and every lag is strictly positive. Exact at any dt. Bin CENTRES -- the centred path's convention -- would be anti-causal by up to dt/2.
one_sided_kernel.second_forward_read_found_and_fixed: knn_rate() used lo = i - k//2, i.e. k/2 prints on EACH side of t, so lambda_hat and therefore s_min(t) and therefore which scale s* the booleans are read at depended on prints that had not happened yet. Swapping only the estimator would have left a forward read in the scale selection. causal=True uses k/(t - t_{i-k}). Reported, not silently fixed.
one_sided_kernel.comparison_discipline: same frozen cohort and hash, same D7 anchors, same ladder, same debounce, same tolerance rule, same 200-draw circular-shift null, same window. ONE THING CHANGES AT A TIME. Event attrition between arms is counted by reason and reported.
one_sided_kernel.tests: research/scale_field/test_onesided.py -- 13 assertions. The causality assertion is checked for BIT EQUALITY by rewriting the future (same array length, so numpy's pairwise summation associates identically); the deletion variant is 4e-15 and the reason is recorded.

result.verdict: D22's structural fact 2 DOES NOT SURVIVE. The ordering reverses.

paired_control.why: the 19 causal contributors are a STRICT SUBSET of the centred 45, so the comparison runs WITHIN event and the population explanation is excluded
paired_control.not_a_special_subpopulation: centred median on the shared 19 is -0.187 vs -0.209 on its other 26

result.unchanged: saturation (dL/dln s >= -1) holds under the causal kernel too; ON 23.4% vs LEVEL 11.9%. D channel fires its kill condition again: median D -1.284 decades, 3 and 2 onsets over 78 events.
result.decisive_open_gap: Under a causal kernel dL/dln s weights RECENT lags while lambda_hat averages the whole half-kernel, centroid s*sqrt(2/pi) = 0.80*s. So a SHORTER LEVEL KERNEL might buy the same lead. Measured lead +1.52 is ~2x the 0.80 centroid gap, so not purely that -- but only the FIXED-KERNEL CONTROL (step_3_recovery_grid, Task 3) separates them. D22 declined Task 3 because the onset test was negative; it is no longer negative, so that reasoning lapses and Task 3 is now DECISIVE.
result.limits_that_must_be_cited_with_the_resul: only 19 of 100 cohort events contribute a matched onset; matched share of LEVEL onsets 20.0% against a 65.1% circular-shift null, so the two booleans are temporally segregated on most events. The null gives 50.0% field-first, so the SIGN is not a selection artifact, but the base is 19 events.
